json.description:
# The Scriptorium as JSON ("{format}", version {version})

What the import does:
The Scriptorium is the place for writing: your own texts ("text" — sermons, talks, reflections, chapters), their deliveries ("delivery"), projects ("project" — a book, a series) and your own text types ("texttype"). A text cites sources from the Library (works, quotes, persons — format "{library}") and points to entries in Learning (e.g. a mystery, a dictionary word, a view); nothing points the other way to the Scriptorium.
- Each entry is { "id", "kind", "key", "data" }. An entry with an id from an export (or with the key of an existing entry of the same kind) is CHANGED — only the fields given in "data"; fields that are absent stay. To clear a field, give null.
- An entry without an id (or with an unknown one) is created. The import deletes nothing.
- References can be ids or keys: "@kazanie-chleb", "@ratzinger2007". Keys from the same document work too.
- A file with works, quotes, persons, comments or topics is rejected — with a note where to import it.
- Who sees an entry is decided only by the area of the scriptorium: the members of the area, and when the area is public — everyone. A text becomes public when it is moved to the scriptorium of a public area (it keeps its id).
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.

{
  "format": "{format}",
  "version": {version},
  "name": "My scriptorium",
  "entries": [ { "kind": "texttype", "key": "kazanie-maryjne", "data": { … } }, { "kind": "text", "data": { … } }, … ]
}

## Kinds of entries
{kinds}

## A text type and its fields
A text type ("texttype") is a name and the extra fields every text of this type has — besides the fixed text fields (title, date, plan, content …). Fields are described like the fields of a kind in Learning: {"key", "label", "type", "multi", "options", "to", "locator", "says"}; "type": {types}.
- "ref" — a reference: "to" are the names of kinds in Learning (e.g. ["Mystery"]) or "work", "quote", "person" (Library) and "text" (another text); "locator": true — with a place.
- A text of this type: "textType": "@type-key", and the field values as ordinary fields in "data" — under the key of the field. A reference to an entry in Learning can be given by its id or its NAME ("Annunciation"); a reference with a place: {"value": "@bt", "locator": "Łk 1,26-38"}; several values ("multi": true) — a list.
- The keys of the fixed text fields are taken: {coreKeys}.
- A text without a type is an ordinary text.

Example — the type “Marian sermon” and one sermon of this type (with Holy Scripture "@bt" from the Library):
{example}

{markup}

## Place in a source
{bible}

## How the app uses this data
- In the Scriptorium the entries stand in the tabs “Texts”, “Deliveries”, “Projects” and “Text types”; a text has an editor (Plan · Content · Further information) with a preview, and its deliveries beside it.
- A text is read with its plan, content, footnotes to Library sources and the list “Sources” at the end; the values of its type's fields stand in the header (“Mystery: Annunciation”).
- A delivery points to the plan's points by their "id": chosen at the text, it shows on the plan what was said, what was only mentioned, what was skipped (with the time in the recording) and what was added. Deliveries stand newest first; in the archive the date of a text is its last delivery.
- On pages: the module “Text from the scriptorium” (one text — plan, deliveries with recording, content, sources) and “Text archive” (the texts of the scriptorium or of one project; search and filters by the reference fields of text types and by projects). A page shows the entry itself, not a copy: a correction in the Scriptorium is at once on every page.
- Printing via LaTeX: a text as an article, a project as a book (texts in the order of "outline"), the plan alone as the “Pulpit plan”.
- A knowledge base that has this scriptorium among its sources takes its entries as material: a text type is a kind of entry there, and card templates and reviews can reach for texts; nothing is copied there. “Review from this text” makes a review there of what the text points to (e.g. quotes, comments, dictionary words).
- In a school a project with "projectType": "program" and "classes" is a curriculum: the texts of its "outline" are lessons, and a delivery with "classArea" — a lesson in a class (Class register, “Delivery in classes”).
- Entries are sealed in the browser with the area's key. “AI access” (the area's link, MCP server), if it covers this scriptorium, gives the assistant a copy to read: texts, deliveries, projects and text types; the assistant changes nothing.

prompt.deliveryBody:
Compare what was said with the plan:
- For EVERY point of the plan give "state": "said" — said (fully or almost), "short" — only mentioned, briefly, "skipped" — skipped.
- "at": when the point starts in the recording (m:ss or h:mm:ss) — only if it was said and you have the recording.
- "note": one short sentence, in the language of the sermon, on what was different from the plan (e.g. another example, another order) — only if something was different.
- "added": what was said but is not in the plan — each thing separately: "text" (one or two sentences), "at", "after" (the id of the point after which it was said).
- "summary": two or three sentences — what mattered most this time.
- "duration": the length of the recording (m:ss).
- "transcript": a full word-for-word transcript, paragraphs separated by an empty line — only if you can transcribe it from the recording; otherwise leave it out.
- Use EXACTLY the point ids in square brackets. Do not change the plan.

{plans}

prompt.plan:
Below is the text of the sermon “{title}”. Make a plan from it: the main thoughts in order, and under each — quotes, examples, questions, applications.

Rules:
- One point — one thought, one or two sentences, in the language of the text, in the order of the text.
- "depth": 0 — main thought, 1 — under it, 2 — deeper still.
- "kind": "thought", "quote", "example", "question", "application".
- Copy references to sources exactly as they stand in the text: [@key, place] or ![@quote-key]. Do not invent new keys.
- Do not add anything that is not in the text.

How the app uses this data:
- The plan goes into the form of this text and replaces the current one; each point gets a lasting id.
- Deliveries mark points by their ids: said, only mentioned, skipped — with the time in the recording. Marks made for the previous plan stay with the delivery, and its form warns that those points are no longer in the plan (they can be removed).
- The plan stands before the content of the text — in the Scriptorium, on pages and in print (also alone, as the “Pulpit plan”); [@key, place] in a point becomes a footnote.

Text:

{body}
---
